<noinclude><pagequality level="4" user="Yann" />{{rh|162|AITAREYA-ÂRA''N''YAKA.|}}{{rule}}</noinclude><section begin="aranyaka1 adhyaya1" />for the Pra-uga. Verily, Anush''t''ubh is valour, and it serves for obtaining valour.'

Others say: 'Let him take a B''ri''hatî hymn for the Pra-uga. Verily, B''ri''hatî is fortune, and thus the sacrificer becomes fortunate.'

Others say: 'Let him take a Paṅkti hymn for the Pra-uga. Verily, Pankti is food, and thus the sacrificer becomes rich in food.'

Others say : 'Let him take a Trish''t''ubh hymn for the Pra-uga. Verily, Trish''t''ubh is strength, and thus the sacrificer becomes strong.'

Others say: ' Let him take a ''G''agatî hymn for the Pra-uga. Verily, cattle is ''G''agatî-like, and thus the sacrificer becomes rich in cattle.'

3. But we say: 'Let him take a ''G''âyatrî hymn only. Verily, ''G''âyatrî is Brahman, and that day (the mahâvrata) is (for the attainment of) Brahman. Thus he obtains Brahman by means of Brahman.

4. 'And it must be a ''G''âyatrî hymn by Madhu''kkh''andas,

5. 'For Madhu''kkh''andas is called Madhu''kkh''andas, because he wishes (''kh''andati) for honey (madhu) for the ''Ri''shis.

6. 'Now food verily is honey, all is honey, all desires are honey, and thus if he recites the hymn of Madhu''kkh''andas, it serves for the attainment of all desires.

7. 'He who knows this, obtains all desires.'

This (Gâyatrî pra-uga), according to the one-day (ekâha) ceremonial<ref>It is copied from the Vi''s''va''g''it, and that from the Agnish''t''oma.</ref> is perfect in form<ref>Nothing is wanting for its performance, if one only follows the rules given in the Agnish''t''oma.</ref>. On that day (the mahâvrata) much is done now and then which<section end="aranyaka1 adhyaya1" /><noinclude>{{rule}}{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>
